notes.conventions: Btu figures are per US short ton as printed; DERIVED conversions use 1 Btu = 1055.06 J and 1 short ton = 0.907185 t. tce = tonne of standard coal equivalent taken as 29.3 GJ. PDF page numbers are the printed page numbers. All 'verified': true entries were read in the fetched text of the cited URL; DERIVED entries quote the inputs read there.
cautions: Raabe 2023 Table 5 (Norgate & Rankin) figures are life-cycle totals with black-coal electricity, not plant energy.
The HPAL 600–900 kg/t acid figure comes from a comparison table in a research paper and is higher than figures usually quoted for operating plants; treat as low confidence.
The PGM row in PMC13514571 mixes 'per kg Pt' and 'per kg PGM' bases as printed.

DOE 'Energy and Environmental Profile' model-mine tables (SHERPA) give equipment energy per ton of material; the Table 5-4 electrowinning value (5.80 Btu/ton) is clearly not a real SX-EW energy and was not used.
Wikipedia's Pidgeon 17–20 kWh/kg statement conflicts in kind with the thermal (coal) basis of the Chinese figures; kept in 'more' only.
